text:
ana: Heads-up — noticed weird provisional token spikes in the console for customer `acme-corp` during last canary. Looks like streaming + fallback + toolcall truncation produced provisional entries that never reconciled.

matt: Ugh. Can you paste the repro or logs?

ana: Quick log excerpt: 
```
INFO router: session_id=83c9a2 parent_session=none route=eu-west-1 model=base-7b
WARN runtime: fallback to quantized-v2 due to OOM
INFO stream: client_eof after 1960ms
ERROR toolcall: truncate invoked, tool=webfetch, reason=client_timeout
METRIC provisional_tokens=142 confirmed_tokens=0 ledger_id=ldg_9b2
```

kai: Looks like provisional ledger was created at stream start, then fallback spun up a new session/ledger and the confirm path never wired back to the original ledger. Reconciler can't match them.

olivia: Is this the case where router generates a fresh session_id on fallback? If so we lose correlation unless we pass the original session as a parent.

matt: Reusing the same ledger across retries could be risky — if fallback goes to a more expensive model we need to bill for the extra tokens separately. We need a safe dedupe heuristic, not blind reuse.

ana: The customer-facing problem is the console: SRE/finance see a provisional spike then a sudden drop. They assume double-billing happened. We need better observability ASAP.

billing-bot: Deploy queued: `billing/reconciler-trace` patch by @olivia (PR 4321) — running CI. :rocket:

kai: Proposal: router emits `X-rl-parent-session` header when it creates a fallback, holding the original session_id. Runtime and billing should emit both `ledger_id` and `parent_session` in metrics. Reconciler should join by (parent_session, model_variant) within a grace window instead of strict ledger equality.

matt: Telemetry additions: routing.fallback=true, toolcall.truncated=true, trace.retry_parent=<id>. Add these tags to spans and to the metric label set. The reconciler should de-dup only if parent_session matches and model_variant is same OR if fallback_reason==soft (like OOM -> quantized with equivalent cost).

olivia: Edge case: fallback to a larger model (downgrade vs upgrade) — parent-based dedupe would incorrectly hide real additional cost. So use a dedupe key (parent_session, model_variant). If model_variant differs, treat as separate billing unless cost_estimate delta < threshold.

ana: For the console UX: add a provisional column in the token breakdown chart and a small tooltip: "Provisional tokens are an initial estimate until the stream/toolcall completes; they may be reconciled." Also add a "fallback reason" label in the per-route timeline. That should defuse the "double-bill" alarms.

kai: Implementation plan:
- router: attach `X-rl-parent-session` and `X-rl-fallback-reason` (kai)
- runtime: include parent_session and provisional flag in ledger events (matt)
- reconciler: dedupe by (parent_session, model_variant) within 10s grace window; emit reconciliation_timeline metrics (matt)
- console: show provisional vs confirmed bars + fallback reason tooltip (olivia)
- infra test: e2e harness for client timeout + fallback + truncated toolcall (ana)

matt: Also add an audit metric `provisional_unresolved_count` and alert when unresolved stays > 0 for > 30m for a given account.

olivia: I'll start the console PR after the reconciler schema is final. Putting up a short doc in docs/console/notes about what provisional means.

ana: I'll add the harness and a short script to simulate client EOF on stream: `curl -v --max-time 2` against the canary route and assert provisional metrics appear then reconcile.

kai: Small logging suggestion: include both `parent_session` and `ledger_id` on WARN/Error lines so we can grep. Example: `WARN runtime: toolcall truncate session=83c9a2 parent=83c9a2 ledger=ldg_9b2 reason=client_timeout`.

matt: Sounds solid. I'll own reconciler changes and tests. Can we get ownership on rollout? I propose canary for 24h with metrics watch.

olivia: +1 on canary. I'll coordinate with product for the console change and add the tooltip copy.

ana: Thanks all — opening follow-up issues and a tracking board in eng-platform.

olivia: :thumbsup:
